name.text: Equation of a wave after transformations

questiontext.text:
The graph of \(y = {@fname@}\,x\) is transformed by, in order:

  1. a stretch with the \(x\)-axis invariant, stretch factor \({@ad@}\);
  2. a stretch with the \(y\)-axis invariant, stretch factor \({@k@}\);
  3. a translation by the vector \(\begin{pmatrix} {@h@}^\circ \\ {@d@} \end{pmatrix}\).

Write the equation of the final graph.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Apply the transformations in turn.

  1. Multiply by \({@ad@}\): \(y = {@ad@}{@fname@}\,x\).
  2. Replace \(x\) by \(\dfrac{x}{{@k@}} = {@bb@}x\): \(y = {@step2@}\).
  3. Replace \(x\) by \(x - ({@h@}^\circ)\) and add \({@d@}\): \(y = {@tunexp@}\), that is \(y = {@ta@}\) (angles in degrees).

questiondescription.text:
Trigonometry III: equation of a wave after transformations

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.5: Apply two stretches and a translation in order to y = sin x or y = cos x and write the equation of the image.

Core

This question is adapted from Example 3 and Question 2 in Exercise B of Chapter 3 of Instone, S., Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP AS/A2 Mathematics: Core 3 for AQA, Cambridge University Press, 2005: applied to sine and cosine waves in degrees with three transformations, randomised over a curated list, any equivalent equation accepted and named feedback added.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: You subtracted \({@h@}^\circ\) from the whole angle. The translation comes after the stretch, so it is \(x\) itself that is replaced by \(x - ({@h@}^\circ)\), in a bracket, in \(y = {@step2@}\).
A stretch with the \(y\)-axis invariant, stretch factor \({@k@}\), replaces \(x\) by \(\dfrac{x}{{@k@}}\), that is \({@bb@}x\), not \({@k@}x\).
A translation of \({@h@}^\circ\) along the \(x\)-axis replaces \(x\) by \(x - ({@h@}^\circ)\).

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="ownok"]]

Test your equation on two points that you can follow through the three transformations. \(({@sx1@}^\circ, 1)\) on \(y = {@fname@}\,x\) is carried to \(({@nice(X1)@}^\circ, {@nice(Y1)@})\); at \(x = {@nice(X1)@}^\circ\) your equation gives \(y = {@nice(own1)@}\). \(({@sx0@}^\circ, 0)\) is carried to \(({@nice(X0)@}^\circ, {@nice(Y0)@})\); at \(x = {@nice(X0)@}^\circ\) your equation gives \(y = {@nice(own0)@}\). The final graph passes through both image points.

[[/if]]

Apply the transformations in turn, each one to the equation you have so far.

qtest.description: Correct: written the other way round
